    This discovery is why Einstein was history’s greatest physicist | by Ethan Siegel | Starts With A Bang! | Sep, 2026
    2 weeks ago
    Ethan Siegel · Medium
    Astrophysicist & science writer
    Einstein is a popular example of a genius. Yet, polymaths like Gauss, Euler, Hamilton, Van Neumann seem far more formidable. Is it just that relativity is remarkable, or am I just impressed by major contributions to wildly different areas?
    Popular comment · It's true that being in the photographic worldwide media era helped Einstein, but also that formidableness is not the only metric. I think lay people are too impressed with smarts as strength, being able to calculate difficult things (as von Neumann could) or learn a lot very quickly. Von Neumann and Hamilton did make major contributions, but Einstein's were more fundamental and caused a surprising rethinking of a lot that seemed very basic and settled. Compare also how David Hilbert and Alexander Grothendeick made arguably more important contributions than von Neumann, but von Neumann has a special charisma among some math and physics followers because he was "formidable". Gauss and Riemann's works are in my opinion also worthy of fame and celebration--as were Maxwell's and Faraday's.

    Albert Einstein’s PhD thesis was not about relativity. In 1905, at age 26, Einstein submitted a 17-page dissertation titled A New Determination of Molecular Dimensions to the University of Zurich. Using the viscosity and diffusion of sugar solutions, he developed a method to calculate molecular sizes and Avogadro’s number. At a time when the existence of atoms was still debated, Einstein found a way to measure the invisible. The dissertation became one of his most frequently cited scientific works.

    Description

    Albert Einstein was a German-born theoretical physicist best known for developing the theory of relativity. Einstein also made important contributions to quantum theory. His mass–energy equivalence formula E = mc², which arises from special relativity, has been called "the world's most famous equation". Wikipedia
    Born: March 14, 1879, Ulm, Germany
    Died: April 18, 1955 (age 76 years), Princeton Medical Center, Plainsboro Township, NJ
    Spouse: Elsa Einstein (m. 1919–1936), Mileva Marić (m. 1903–1919)
    Children: Eduard Einstein, Lieserl Einstein, Hans Albert Einstein
    Education: University of Zurich (1905), ETH Zürich (1897–1900) · See more
    Height: 5′ 9″
    Parents: Hermann Einstein, Pauline Einstein
